title: Tuga A6 vs Tuga A10: Pocket Handheld or 10 Inch Site Tablet?
description: Tuga A6 handheld (£299) or Tuga A10 tablet (£449), £150 apart. Pocket proof of delivery and photos, or a 10.1 inch screen for plans. Or one of each.
summary: The A6 is £150 cheaper, pocketable, better sealed and has 5G; the A10 has the 10.1 inch Full HD screen for drawings, plans and spreadsheets.
lede: If you are choosing between the smallest and largest Tuga Android devices, buy the Tuga A6 (£299) for proof of delivery, photos and job sheets from a pocket, or the Tuga A10 (£449) to read plans on site. If your firm does both jobs, buy one of each.
verdict: Buy the Tuga A6 at £299 unless you read plans or drawings on site, in which case buy the Tuga A10 at £449. The £150 gap buys screen area, not a better specification: 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 against 6.78 inches at 2460 x 1080, so the A10 is bigger but no sharper. The A6 is a handheld for a pocket or a belt holster; the A10 is a tablet for a vehicle mount or a site office. Both run Android 14, are sealed to IP68, list MIL-STD-810H and are rated from -20°C to 60°C, so the question is how much screen the job needs. Proof of delivery, photos, job sheets, sign-off and comms fit on the A6. Blueprints, PDF plans, BIM viewers and full spreadsheets are easier on the A10.

Keep the £150 if a phone-sized screen will do, because the A6 is the better specified device in most of the table. It has 5G where the A10 has 4G, IP69K on top of IP68 for jet washing, a 10600mAh battery with 33W fast charging against 8000mAh, and 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage against 8GB and 128GB. It is also brighter (560 nits against 350) and lighter (441g against 680g).

Pay the £150 when the screen is the job. The A10 gives you a 10.1 inch Full HD screen to read a drawing without pinching and zooming, dual SIM 4G for rural sites where one network is patchy, a hand strap in the box and a 3.5mm headphone jack. The Charging Dock (£49.99) and Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) are listed for the A10 and not the A6. At 350 nits it is also the dimmer screen, so if you read plans outdoors all day, look at the 800 nit Tuga A8 at £379 first. If your firm does both jobs, buy one of each. Check that the apps you rely on run on the device before you order.
chooseA: Your day is proof of delivery, photos, job sheets and sign-off, and you want one device in a pocket or a Belt Holster (£22): 441g against 680g.
You upload from site and want 5G rather than 4G, with a 10600mAh battery and 33W fast charging to get through a long shift.
The device gets jet washed with the van: IP68 plus IP69K against IP68 alone on the A10.
You photograph lofts, voids, loading bays and doorsteps after dark, where the 64MP night vision camera beats the A10's 13MP.
You work outdoors with gloves on: the A6 has glove mode and a 560 nit screen against 350, plus a fingerprint sensor and face unlock that the A10 does not list.
chooseB: You read drawings, PDF plans, BIM models or full spreadsheets on site: 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 against 6.78 inches on the A6.
You want it on the dashboard or in a desk dock: the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) and Charging Dock (£49.99) are listed for the A10 and not the A6. The A6 takes the Car Phone Mount (£17) instead.
You work on rural sites where one network is patchy: the A10 has dual SIM 4G, so two networks can be fitted.
You want a stylus for detail work with the gloves off: the Capacitive Stylus (£14.99) is listed for the A10 and not the A6, and a hand strap is in the box.
You run a fleet of ten or more and want a swap unit service: the quote-only Total Care plan is offered on the A10 and not the A6.

faq.q: Is the Tuga A10 worth £150 more than the Tuga A6?
faq.a: Only if you need the screen. The A10 costs £449 and the A6 £299. The A6 has 5G, IP69K, the bigger battery, more RAM and storage, the brighter screen and the higher resolution camera. What the £150 buys is a 10.1 inch Full HD screen, dual SIM 4G, a headphone jack and a pogo pin connector, and the dock and vehicle mount are listed for it. If you read plans, drawings or spreadsheets on site, the screen is worth £150 on its own; if you do not, buy the Tuga A6. Both have 12 months of warranty included and can take the paid 3-Year Warranty at £65 each.

faq.q: Should a small firm buy one of each?
faq.a: If your firm does both jobs, yes. The A6 and the A10 do different jobs, so a firm whose drivers or engineers take photos and signatures while someone else reads the plans is not choosing between them and needs both. Put the A6 with whoever is on the doorstep and in the loft, and the A10 with whoever works from drawings, on the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) or in the cabin. Bulk discounts count devices across models, so one A6 and one A10 qualifies, and the tiers are on the bulk page. The 12V DC Car Charger (£26), the USB-C to USB-A OTG Adapter (£8) and the Tempered Glass Screen Protector (2 Pack, £14) are listed for both devices, so one accessories order covers a mixed pair; see accessories.

faq.q: Can I read drawings on the A6 instead of buying the A10?
faq.a: For a quick look it may be enough; for working from a plan all day, no. The A6 screen is 6.78 inches at 2460 x 1080. Whether a PDF is comfortable to read for a quick dimension or cable route depends on your own app, so try it on the device. Working through a set of drawings, a BIM viewer or a full spreadsheet means constant pinching, zooming and scrolling, which is where the A10's 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 helps most. Open the biggest drawing you use on a normal day and see whether you can work from it. One thing to weigh the other way: at 350 nits the A10 has the dimmer screen, so in direct sun it is harder to read than the A6 at 560 nits. If you read plans outdoors more than indoors, the 800 nit Tuga A8 at £379 is the one to look at next.

faq.q: Which is tougher, the A6 or the A10?
faq.a: They share IP68, MIL-STD-810H and the -20°C to 60°C rating. The A6 lists more protection on top: IP69K, which survives jet washing rather than just rain, and Gorilla Glass 5; the A10 lists tempered glass. Neither lists a drop height or which tests were run. The A10 is a slim 14.5mm and 680g, so it is more likely to travel in a bag or a mount than a pocket, and the Rugged Carry Case (£34) suits it; the A6 at 441g rides in a Belt Holster (£22). Our IP rating guide and MIL-STD-810H guide explain what each rating does and does not test.
